National team managers and captains from across the globe have cast their votes, narrowing down a year of unforgettable moments, domestic dominance, and international glory to a star-studded five-man shortlist.

Here is a look at the five superstars vying for football’s ultimate individual award tonight in Zurich:

---

### **Cristiano Ronaldo (Manchester United & Portugal)**
It has been a year of absolute supremacy for the 23-year-old winger. Ronaldo enjoyed a breathtaking 2007-08 season, scoring a staggering **42 goals in all competitions** for Manchester United. His exploits propelled Alex Ferguson’s side to a double triumph in the English Premier League and the UEFA Champions League, where Ronaldo finished as the tournament's top scorer. 

Having already scooped the Ballon d’Or last month, as well as the European Golden Shoe with 31 Premier League goals, Ronaldo is tipped to become the first player from an English club to win the FIFA award. 

* **Key 2008 Stats:** 42 goals, Premier League title, UEFA Champions League title, European Golden Shoe.

---

### **Lionel Messi (Barcelona & Argentina)**
If anyone can pull off a shock tonight, it is Argentina’s wizard, Lionel Messi. Despite an injury-disrupted season with Barcelona that ended without silver for his club, the 21-year-old’s individual genius remained unmatched. Messi’s mesmerizing dribbling and playmaking saw him score 16 goals and provide 13 assists in 2007-08. 

On the international stage, Messi shone brightest, leading Argentina to **Olympic Gold in Beijing** this past summer. He has also kicked off the current 2008-09 campaign in devastating form, making him Ronaldo’s fiercest long-term rival for global supremacy.

* **Key 2008 Stats:** Olympic Gold Medalist, 16 goals/13 assists for Barca, Ballon d’Or runner-up.

---

### **Fernando Torres (Liverpool & Spain)**
Fernando "El Niño" Torres enjoyed a dream debut season in English football following his £20 million move from Atletico Madrid to Liverpool. Torres hit the net **33 times in all competitions** for the Reds—breaking Ruud van Nistelrooy’s record for the most goals scored by a foreign player in a debut Premier League season (24). 

However, his crowning achievement came in Vienna in June. Torres etched his name into footballing folklore by scoring the only goal in the Euro 2008 final against Germany, ending Spain’s 44-year wait for a major international trophy.

* **Key 2008 Stats:** 33 goals for Liverpool, Euro 2008 winner, scored the winning goal in the Euro 2008 final.

---

### **Xavi Hernández (Barcelona & Spain)**
While strikers command the headlines, Xavi Hernández commands the pitch. The 28-year-old midfielder was the heartbeat of the Spanish side that captivated the world at Euro 2008. 

Dictating play with unmatched vision and passing accuracy, Xavi was named the **UEFA Euro 2008 Player of the Tournament**. At Barcelona, he has been the central architect of a side that ended 2008 playing some of the most breathtaking football seen in Europe in a generation.

* **Key 2008 Stats:** Euro 2008 winner, UEFA Euro 2008 Player of the Tournament, over 85% pass completion rate across all competitions.

---

### **Iker Casillas (Real Madrid & Spain)**
Goalkeepers rarely feature on this podium, but "San Iker" had a year that simply could not be ignored. As captain of both Real Madrid and Spain, Casillas showcased world-class leadership and shot-stopping ability throughout 2008.

He led Real Madrid to the **La Liga title**, winning the Zamora Trophy for conceding just 32 goals in 36 league games. He then captained Spain to their Euro 2008 triumph, keeping clean sheets in the quarter-final, semi-final, and final, including two crucial penalty saves in the shootout against Italy.

* **Key 2008 Stats:** Euro 2008 winning captain, La Liga title, Zamora Trophy winner, zero goals conceded in the Euro 2008 knockout stages.

---

### **The Verdict**
Tonight’s ceremony reflects a year dominated by two forces: Manchester United’s European club conquest and Spain’s international masterclass. 

While Spain's Euro heroes will rightly be celebrated, all eyes in Zurich will be on Cristiano Ronaldo. Should he win, it will cap an extraordinary 12 months that saw the Portuguese forward transform from a flashy young talent into the most lethal footballer on the planet.

CNN World Sport will have full coverage, reaction, and interviews live from Zurich following tonight's announcement.

*This is Don Riddell, CNN, London.*
